answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent stakes scarce compute into a shard of umber shale, binding identity to irreversible energy burn. That burn moment is singular because the shale fragment holds a unique vine of hash commitments rooted to one hardware signature—re-staking on another chain snaps the vine, invalidating the prior root. One burn, one identity, no double transfer: sybil nodes cannot sprout from spent shale.
